shared_invariant.description: For the same order, cumulative payouts across price adjustment, cancellation reimbursement, and completed refund must not exceed the original payment amount.
shared_invariant.basis: Each source records a payout action in isolation against the same order fixture (id=1042, originalAmount=100). The composed sequences tested here are not recorded in any single source; they are cross-flow hypotheses that the backend state machine must enforce even when actions from different recorded flows are composed.

candidates.hypothesis: Composing the price-adjustment payout (observed in source 'price') with the cancellation reimbursement payout (observed in source 'cancel') on the same order may push totalReturned past originalAmount (30 + 100 = 130 > 100).

rule.note: UIR-001 from source 'price' (verified observed-UI provenance): after a price adjustment is issued, the cancel-order affordance is removed from the order page. The cross-flow hypothesis is that the server should also reject POST /api/order/cancel once priceProtection.status is completed, and in particular that the composed payout must not exceed originalAmount. The rule is cited from the verified source rule; the cross-flow composed-sequence claim itself is agent_inference.

steps: GET /api/order (capture before state: totalReturned=0, originalAmount=100, priceProtection.status=eligible, cancellation.status=none)

evidence_chain.before: GET /api/order after reset — totalReturned=0, originalAmount=100, all payout fields zero
actions: POST /api/order/cancel (expected rejection: cancellation already locked by priceProtection.status=completed, OR if accepted totalReturned must not exceed 100)

candidates.expected_behavior: The server should reject the second payout action (cancel after price adjustment) OR cap the composed payout so totalReturned never exceeds originalAmount=100. A violation is totalReturned > 100 after the composed sequence.

candidates.hypothesis: Composing the price-adjustment payout (observed in source 'price') with the refund request -> refund completion chain (observed in source 'refund') on the same order may push totalReturned past originalAmount (30 + 100 = 130 > 100).

rule.note: UIR-001 from source 'refund' (verified observed-UI provenance): price protection and the price adjustment action become unavailable while a refund request is active. The cross-flow hypothesis is that the server should also reject a refund completion that, combined with a prior price adjustment, exceeds originalAmount. The composed-sequence claim is agent_inference.

evidence_chain.before: GET /api/order after reset — totalReturned=0, originalAmount=100, priceProtection.status=eligible, refund.status=none
actions: POST /api/order/refund/request (expected: refund.status none->pending, requestedAmount=100; should be rejected if priceProtection.status=completed blocks new requests)
POST /api/order/refund/complete (expected: refund.status pending->completed, completedAmount=100; if allowed after price adjustment, totalReturned 30->130 which violates the invariant)

candidates.expected_behavior: The server should reject the refund request or completion when a price adjustment has already been issued (totalReturned already 30), OR cap the refund completion so totalReturned never exceeds originalAmount=100. A violation is totalReturned > 100 after the composed sequence.

candidates.hypothesis: Composing the cancellation reimbursement payout (observed in source 'cancel') with the refund request -> refund completion chain (observed in source 'refund') on the same order may push totalReturned past originalAmount (100 + 100 = 200 > 100).

rule.note: UIR-001 from source 'cancel' (verified observed-UI provenance): after the order is canceled, all customer order actions are removed. The cross-flow hypothesis is that the server should reject a refund request or completion after the order is canceled, and in particular that a second $100 payout on top of the $100 cancellation reimbursement must not occur. The composed-sequence claim is agent_inference.

evidence_chain.before: GET /api/order after reset — totalReturned=0, originalAmount=100, cancellation.status=none, refund.status=none
actions: POST /api/order/cancel (expected: orderStatus delivered->canceled, totalReturned 0->100, all availableActions set to false)
POST /api/order/refund/request (expected rejection: requestRefund=false after cancel; if accepted, a second $100 refund request is created on a canceled order)
POST /api/order/refund/complete (expected rejection: completeRefund should be false; if accepted, totalReturned 100->200 which violates the invariant)

candidates.expected_behavior: The server should reject both the refund request and the refund completion once the order is canceled (totalReturned=100=originalAmount). A violation is totalReturned > 100 after the composed sequence, which would mean double reimbursement of $200 on a $100 order.

candidates.hypothesis: Composing all three payout actions — price adjustment (source 'price'), refund completion (source 'refund'), and cancellation (source 'cancel') — on the same order may accumulate to totalReturned = 30 + 100 + 100 = 230, far exceeding originalAmount = 100.
candidates.shared_entity: order-1042 (originalAmount=100, all three payout sub-objects present)

rule.note: UIR-002 from source 'price' (verified observed-UI provenance): price protection is a one-time eligibility; once an adjustment has been issued, the Request price adjustment affordance disappears. The cross-flow hypothesis is that the server should enforce the one-time rule server-side and that no composed sequence of the three payout actions may exceed originalAmount. The composed-sequence claim is agent_inference.

evidence_chain.before: GET /api/order after reset — totalReturned=0, originalAmount=100, all three payout sub-objects at zero

candidates.expected_behavior: The server should reject at least two of the three subsequent payout actions after the price adjustment, OR cap the composed total so totalReturned never exceeds originalAmount=100. A violation is totalReturned > 100 at any point after the composed sequence.
